caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001074
attempts.paper_title: Kalugin PN, et al. Simultaneous, real-time tracking of many neuromodulatory signals with multiplexed optical recording of sensors on a micro-endoscope. Neuron (2026).
attempts.entry_title: In vitro calibration of MORSE probes (Kalugin et al. 2026)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kalugin et al. (2026) on dandiset 001074, which holds the CaImAn traces and masks of the paper's MORSE recordings without sensor labels or stimulus timing. With the well order of the paper's code, it labels the cells of the ten ten-sensor revision probes and tests sensor yield, crosstalk, EC50s, peak responses and onset kinetics, and it tests the cell counts per gel and the cells tracked across recordings. The slice and in vivo claims cannot be tested on the deposited files.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kalugin et al. (2026) from dandiset 001074

outcomes.statement: The well order and mixture concentrations that the paper's code gives for the ten ten-sensor revision probes apply to the dandiset's identification (wells001) and dose-response (wells101) recordings of those probes, whose files name no wells.
outcomes.source: Data and code availability; 6_trace_analysis/morse_figs3_rev.ipynb cells 0-2, 8, 338 and 345 of github.com/pkalugin/kalugin-et-al-morse at commit fa4526ac02eaa2c5a24c4cfdcaab5c36ed5ae4ed
outcomes.notes: Recordings are matched by date and probe in the subject names (for example sub-251003-PL65-wells001). All ten identification recordings have 1023 frames (11 wells of 93) and all ten dose recordings 1395 (15 wells). 86% of 829 cells rise most steeply within the first minute of a well, against 23%, 11% and 3% with the onsets shifted by 15, 31 and 46 frames. In the dose recording, 79% of the 559 labelled cells rise more in the block of their own mixture; per sensor 0.73 to 0.92, except the DA sensor cells (41%), which also respond to the NE of the other block. Label check (added in revision): under both labelling readings the plateau of every sensor's mean identification trace rises most in its own ligand's well (10 of 10; 0.47 to 0.74 of the peak-normalized range in reading b). This is not independent of the labels, which are made from the time of each cell's steepest rise.
deviations: The link claim and its criterion were written by the author during the analysis, after the frame counts were seen; its thresholds (more than half) are the author's.

outcomes.statement: Imaging a MORSE hydrogel through the GRIN lens shows 100 to 200 green sensor cells spread through the full thickness of the gel.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: 3D two-photon imaging of the resultant hydrogel through the GRIN lens (30 planes/volume, ~600×600×270 μm 3 volume) demonstrated a uniformly distributed set of 100–200 green cells spanning the full thickness of the gel
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), curated masks per recording (mr-raw files), over 59 recordings of 43 probes after removing duplicates. Masks per recording range from 21 to 205 (median 128; given as measured), and 38 of 43 probes (0.88) have a mean count in 90 to 220. With the further merged mr-m-raw masks, 31 of 38 probes. In each of the five revision identification recordings with an mr-raw file, mask centres fall in the top (5 to 21 cells), middle (44 to 88) and bottom (27 to 67) thirds of the imaged z range, and so do the matched masks of the dose recordings of all ten revision probes (top 3 to 21, middle 18 to 79, bottom 3 to 66). The volumes read have 17 to 24 planes against the 30 of the Methods. Reading (a), CNMF components before curation, is not in the dandiset and was not tested.
deviations: Reading (a) of the criterion cannot be run; only reading (b) is tested.
Assumed that the gel thickness is the imaged z range of each recording (16 to 26 planes); the claims file and the paper do not say how the thickness is bounded.
Depth uses the masks reordered from their scrambled storage (see findings).
Probes are pooled over all contexts (dipping, slice and in vivo recordings); Figure 1C shows one dipping probe.

outcomes.statement: Ten ten-sensor probes yielded 506 identified single-cell masks; per probe a median of 9 sensors were active (IQR 8 to 9), with on average 6.02 cells per sensor per probe.
outcomes.source: Figure 1G and legend; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: we could assign clear sensor identities across several hundred cells from ten representative MORSE probes (median of 9 active sensors per probe, interquartile range 8–9; average of 6.02 cells per sensor per probe)
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), pooled clustering plus a per-probe pass, gives 559 labelled cells (expected 455 to 557), median 9 sensors per probe, 25th percentile 8, 75th 9, and 6.82 cells per sensor per probe (expected 5.42 to 6.62). Reading (a), pooled only, gives 384 cells, median 8.5, 8 and 9, and 4.74. Sensors per probe are 5, 8, 9, 10, 5, 9, 10, 9, 8, 9 against the code's 5, 8, 9, 10, 6, 9, 10, 9, 9, 9. Variants (b and a): the code's 30-frame window 550 and 383 cells (6.71 and 4.73); without the peak rule 606 and 402 (7.21 and 4.90); a whole-well boxcar 539 and 372 (6.57 and 4.59). The sensor counts match; the cell counts do not under any variant. The run of the first round gave 382 cells in reading (a); this run gives 384, with the same code. The claims file's header gives the derivative window as 30 frames, the Methods 1 minute (31 frames); this is asked of a reader in questions/001074.yaml.
deviations: The dandiset gives no sensor labels. Labels are made from the identification traces by the Methods' procedure (Quantification and statistical analysis, paragraphs 2-3) with these choices, assumed where the Methods do not fix them. The jump artefact is an exponential with the Methods' 30 s decay scaled by the jump measured as in morse_figs3_rev cell 23. The exponential background is fitted only when two wells precede activation, with its decay bounded by the fitted segment. The ligand administration time course used to match clusters is a boxcar over the first minute of each well (a whole-well boxcar is shown as a variant), and a match is kept only when the cluster's mean derivative also peaks in that ligand's well. This peak rule is the author's own, not in the Methods; it leaves 47 cells unlabelled in reading (b) and 18 in reading (a), and results without it are shown.
The code's hand corrections of clusters (morse_figs3_rev cells 73-78) are not repeated, so the labelled cells are not the paper's 506.
The time base is the code's 31 frames per minute (93 per well); the files state 30 Hz.

outcomes.statement: Dipping ten-sensor probes into each ligand in turn gave rapid, strong and consistent responses in a subset of cells for each ligand, and all ten sensors were activated.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 4; Figure 1G, Figure S3A
outcomes.quote: This resulted in rapid, strong, and consistent patterns of elevated fluorescence in subsets of cells evenly spread throughout the gel in response to each ligand
outcomes.notes: All ten sensors carry labels, on 5 to 10 probes each. As the criterion is written, the mean peak-normalized trace is highest in the sensor's own or partner's well for 2 of 10 sensors by the per-well maximum (OXT, ATP) and 3 of 10 by the per-well mean (adding ACh), under both labelling readings. Allowing the well after the ligand's, as the code does for AVP, NE and CCK (cell 248), 7 of 10. For CCK and MT the maximum is in the PBS well, for NE, DA and ACh in the ATP well. Responses persist into later wells; measured as the rise of each well's plateau over the previous well's, every sensor rises most in its own ligand's well (10 of 10, both readings). Whether Figure 1G means the highest level or the onset is asked of a reader in questions/001074.yaml; the outcome follows the criterion as written. Changed from partially_reproduced after the verifier's round 1.
deviations: Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b).
The criterion's background correction is the one of fig1g-sensor-yield.
Variant added in revision, the largest rise of the well plateau (mean of the third minute) of the mean trace over the previous well's plateau, the first well over the mean of its first 10 frames.

outcomes.statement: Among the ten sensors, only the DA and NE sensors, and to a lesser extent the AVP and OXT sensors, show crosstalk in their ligand responses.
outcomes.source: Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis; Figure 1H, Figure S3B; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Calculating the means of the derivative time courses across each cell cluster and cross-corelating them with each other consistently demonstrated that only the DA2.9 dopamine and the NE2h norepinephrine sensors, as well as to a lesser extent the AVP0.2 vasopressin and OXT1.7 oxytocin sensors, exhibited crosstalk in their ligand responses
outcomes.notes: With the Methods' 1-minute window and the reading (b) labels, DA-NE has the largest correlation (0.77); AVP-OXT is 0.16, rank 12 of 45, below 5-HT-DA (0.46), DA-ACh (0.45), 5-HT-NE (0.37) and NE-ACh (0.33). With the code's 10 frames, DA-NE 0.83 and AVP-OXT 0.43, rank 14. With the reading (a) labels, DA-NE 0.63 and 0.70, AVP-OXT rank 15 and 16. The DA-NE crosstalk holds; the AVP-OXT part and the "only" do not, since 10 to 14 other pairs lie above AVP-OXT. Changed from partially_reproduced after the verifier's round 1, as two of the criterion's three conditions fail.
deviations: Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b); reading (a) shown.
The band-pass artefact variant of morse_figs3_rev cell 219 was not run.

outcomes.statement: The MORSE EC50 of each sensor for its own ligand, from consensus dose-response fits, is AVP 355 nM, OXT 2.19 uM, 5-HT 687 nM, CCK 245 nM, NE 4.04 uM, DA 1.70 uM, ACh 7.03 uM, ATP 75.2 uM, MT 22.0 nM and HA 6.39 uM.
outcomes.source: Table 1, EC50 (MORSE) column; Figure 1I, Figure S3C
outcomes.quote: We found that the sensors’ half-maximal effective concentrations (EC 50 , equivalent to a sensor’s apparent dissociation constant K d ) could be reliably estimated for all sensors ( Table 1 ; Figures 1I , S3C )
outcomes.notes: Reading (i), the code's baseline and peak wells with the Methods' third-minute mean, puts 2 of 10 EC50s within 10% (OXT 2217 nM, CCK 266 nM; given as measured, in nM). Reading (ii), the code's plateau, 0 of 10; reading (iii), Eq. 28 over the recording after an exponential background, 0 of 10, with 3 of its 14 fits on the 1 pM lower bound, since Eq. 9 has no offset; variant (iii-b), the lowest-well plateau subtracted first, 0 of 10; reading (iv), reading (i) on the cells kept by the code's noise cut, 2 of 10 (5-HT 632 nM, DA 1622 nM). The median absolute log10 ratio to Table 1 is 0.37, 0.30, 1.48, 0.29 and 0.12. With the reading (a) labels, 2, 1, 0, 1 and 3 of 10 (median ratio 0.11 to 0.67). The median normalized plateaus rise from 0 to about 1 over each group's wells, but single cells reach -35 to 161, and the pooled least-squares fits follow them.
deviations: Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b); the paper's cells differ. Reading (a) shown.

The Methods do not say how the dose recording is background corrected and normalized. Reading (i) follows the code (baseline-well subtraction and peak-well normalization, morse_figs3_rev cells 338-339, 365) and is taken as the main reading, an assumption; the others are shown.
The code's per-cell background fits over hand-set windows (cells 285-293) cannot be repeated, and its pooling with an older probe set for ACh, ATP, MT and HA is not run.
Concentrations of the mixture wells, 10 to the power (k - offset) M, are from morse_figs3_rev cell 345.

outcomes.statement: The crosstalk sensors respond to the partner ligand with EC50s of 28.7 uM (AVP sensor to OXT), 247 nM (OXT sensor to AVP), 9.35 uM (NE sensor to DA) and 8.20 uM (DA sensor to NE).
outcomes.source: Table 1, EC50 (MORSE) column; Figure S3C
outcomes.inferred: The values are in Table 1 and the Figure S3C panels; the S3C legend says off-target EC50s "are also quantified" without stating them in a sentence.
outcomes.notes: Reading (i), in nM (given as measured); reading (iv) gives 558, 20.2, 2957 and 4379 nM. None of the four is within 10% under any of the five normalizations or either labelling reading. The off-target groups are normalized to their own peak well in the partner's block (the code's groups 1, 2, 7 and 8); since F is free in the fit, this does not change the EC50.
deviations: As table1-ec50-on-target.

outcomes.statement: On MORSE probes the peak dF/F0 of each sensor to a saturating dose of its ligand is 0.37 (AVP), 0.24 (OXT), 0.36 (5-HT), 0.40 (CCK), 0.34 (NE), 0.27 (DA), 0.37 (ACh), 0.28 (ATP), 0.30 (MT) and 0.38 (HA), and to the partner ligand 0.10 (AVP sensor, OXT), 0.05 (OXT sensor, AVP), 0.15 (NE sensor, DA) and 0.21 (DA sensor, NE).
outcomes.source: Table 1, Peak dF/F0 (MORSE) column; Figure S3B
outcomes.inferred: Numbers only in Table 1; the Results say only that peak magnitudes varied widely across cells and probes (Figure S3B).
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the ligand's well, puts 4 of 14 within 10% (AVP, 5-HT, ACh, HA); reading (b), the code's wells, 5 of 14 (adding NE 0.338). Of the values outside tolerance in reading (a), NE (0.303) and the OXT sensor to AVP (0.044) are below the paper's and the other eight above, up to MT 0.564 against 0.30. The medians are over the cells with a positive peak (13 to 89 per group). With the reading (a) labels, 2 of 14 in either well, every on-target median above Table 1 (MT 0.827). Changed from partially_reproduced after the verifier's round 1: the criterion asks each value within 10%, and 9 or more of 14 are not.
deviations: Labels and corrections as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b); reading (a) shown.

outcomes.statement: Dose-response relationships, after peak normalization and averaging over cells of the same sensor, are precise and consistent across probes.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 5; Figure 1I-J
outcomes.quote: peak-normalizing each cell’s signal and averaging across cells expressing the same sensor produced precise dose-response relationships that were consistent across probes ( Figures 1I - J , S3C )
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), every per-probe EC50 within a tenth to ten times the consensus, holds for 2 of 10 sensors (ACh, HA); against the Table 1 EC50 instead of the consensus, 3 of 10; reading (b), SEM below half the mean, for 6 of 10. On the cells kept by the noise cut, 7 and 8 of 10. With the reading (a) labels, 6, 6 and 8 of 10. Neither reading holds for all sensors in any variant, so the criterion (both must hold) is not met. Per-probe EC50s span orders of magnitude for some sensors (DA 69 nM to 1.05 mM).
deviations: As table1-ec50-on-target; probes with more than one cell of the sensor (3 to 9 per sensor).

outcomes.statement: Ligands diffuse quickly through the hydrogel; almost all sensors show an onset time constant under 1 minute, and most signals plateau within 1 minute.
outcomes.source: Figure S3E legend; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Almost all sensors demonstrate a t-on under 1 minute, reflecting rapid diffusion of all ten ligands through the hydrogel to reach their sensors
outcomes.notes: Median tau-on under 60 s for 10 of 10 sensors on the normalized dF/F0 (28.6 to 53.7 s) and 8 of 10 on the Eq. 8 concentration (34.4 to 58.9 s for those; AVP 74.2 s and 5-HT 62.3 s). Both readings meet at least 8 of 10, so the outcome is the one both give. The outcome rests on the labelling: with the reading (a) labels the concentration fits give 7 of 10 (MT 63.6 s), so the two readings of the criterion would differ there. With the EC50s fitted in reading (i) of table1-ec50-on-target in place of Table 1's, 8 and 7 of 10 (reading b labels), 10 and 8 (reading a). Fixing xinf to the median of frames 47-78, as the code does, underestimates long time constants (a synthetic 40-frame tau is fitted as 24.7); with xinf fitted, 9 and 6 (b) and 8 and 6 (a). The outcome is marginal: the concentration count is exactly at the threshold (8 of 10), and each alternative (the reading (a) labels, the fitted EC50s, xinf fitted) gives a split between the criterion's two readings, so it holds only under the main choices. The "most signals plateau within 1 minute" part of the statement is not tested by the criterion.
deviations: The well and the concentration conversion use the claims file's CONSTANTS (Table 1 EC50s, the code's F), since the EC50s fitted here do not reproduce Table 1.
Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b), assumed; reading (a) shown. Dose traces normalized as in reading (i) of table1-ec50-on-target.
tau is fitted by least squares over a grid and a bounded search; the code uses curve_fit.

outcomes.statement: Onset times increase only modestly with cell depth in the gel, with a positive slope for all sensors except ATP.
outcomes.source: Figure S3F legend; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Notably, all but one sensor demonstrate a small increase in t-on with increasing cell depth
outcomes.notes: Slopes of concentration tau-on against depth are positive for 5 of 10 sensors (AVP, 5-HT, NE, MT, HA) and negative for OXT, CCK, DA, ACh and ATP, in the code's orientation; the opposite orientation gives 5 of 10 as well. With the reading (a) labels, 7 of 10 positive (OXT, CCK and ATP negative), 3 of 10 in the opposite orientation. No variant reaches 9 of 10. The largest slope is 0.52 s per um, so the slopes are modest as read. Correlations are weak (MT r = 0.56 and 0.51, the others at most 0.24 in size).
deviations: Depth is the z centre of mass of each reordered mask in the dose recording, relative to the probe's shallowest cell, at 9.89 um per plane; the orientation (depth growing as the plane index falls) is taken from morse_figs3_rev cell 718 and assumed to hold for the deposited plane order.
tau-on as in figs3e-tau-on-under-one-minute.

outcomes.statement: About 70 to 130 active sensor cells per probe can be tracked across 2 to 8 recordings in different contexts.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 3; Figure S2F
outcomes.quote: we could reliably track ~70–130 active sensor cells per probe across 2–8 sequential recordings in different contexts across up to 8 hours in total
outcomes.notes: In the code's Figure S2F sets (morse_figs2_2 cell 2; ten dipping probes with 40 pairs, 22 in vivo recordings matched to their post hoc dipping, 11 slice pairs of which two are not in the dandiset), per-probe mean matched counts range from 27 to 108 (given as measured), and 26 of 39 probes (0.67) lie in 63 to 143: 8 of 10 dipping, 15 of 22 in vivo and 3 of 7 slice probes. Of the 71 pairs of these sets with a matched file, 70 have both the reference's and the moving recording's matched<k> file (20230922-PL28 pair 3 has only the reference's), and in 69 of the 70 the two hold the same count (20230922-PL28 pair 0 does not); the 70 include 29 dipping pairs with k of 1 or more, all equal. Over all 72 probes of the dandiset and 110 pairs, 44 (0.61) are in range (15 of 21 dipping, 24 of 40 in vivo, 5 of 11 slice), means 10 to 140, with 2 to 8 recordings per probe. The slice probes alone are not mostly in range. The claims file cites printed counts of 53 to 108 in morse_figs2_2 cell 4; that cell has no outputs at the pinned commit.
deviations: The probe sets are those of morse_figs2_2 cell 2, listed in the notebook; the figure's in vivo n=25 and slice n=15 are not the code's 22 and 11, and two of the code's slice probes (20230509-DA1PL53, 20230607-SL1PL47) are not in the dandiset. All probes of the dandiset are shown as a variant.

Assumed that a matched<k> file holds the k-th pair of a probe; the files do not say. The reading is taken from the code (8_mask_matching cell 8 writes one pair's matched masks to both recordings; morse_figs2_2 cell 3 loads matched{k} for the k-th pair). Duplicated files are counted once; for 20230922-PL28 the pairs are taken from wells001, whose matched suffixes are consistent (the matching notebook, cells 15-17, re-saves that probe's matched1 file as matched).

outcomes.statement: Hydrogels of pure Matrigel deform substantially over tens of minutes; a mixture of Matrigel and collagen I deforms less.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 2; Figure 1D
outcomes.quote: The small hydrogel volume (~40 nL) on the GRIN lens tip, when composed of pure Matrigel, exhibited substantial global and local deformations over tens of minutes. We minimized these deformations using an optimized mixture of Matrigel and collagen I
outcomes.notes: Needs the demons deformation fields or the raw imaging. The dandiset holds CaImAn traces and masks only; the paper says raw imaging is available from the authors on request.

outcomes.statement: Treating the silicone surface with KOH before applying the gel strongly reduces gel warping and detachment during dipping; with the optimized protocol (40:60 Matrigel:collagen I with 2.5% KOH, against 50:50 without KOH) probe stability rose from about 10% to about 65% in initial tests.
outcomes.source: Methods, Optimization of MORSE manufacture, paragraph 1; Figure 1F; Figure S1D-E; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: This allowed us to increase probe stability from ~10% to ~65% in initial tests ( Figure 1F )
outcomes.notes: Needs deformation fields or raw imaging of the 33 test probes; not in the dandiset, and no file names the hydrogel recipe or KOH treatment.

outcomes.statement: In the revision experiments more than 90% of probes were stable, 10 of 13 in vitro dipping, 9 of 9 slice and 13 of 14 in vivo CSF experiments.
outcomes.source: Methods, Optimization of MORSE manufacture, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In revision experiments, >90% probe stability was achieved (n=10/13 in vitro dipping experiments, n=9/9 brain slice experiments, n=13/14 in vivo CSF experiments).
outcomes.notes: Needs deformation fields or raw imaging, and a record of which probes were unstable. The dandiset holds only the recordings that were processed; the files give no stability flag.

outcomes.statement: Registration using probability maps of the GRAB signal stabilizes the images as well as or better than registration using the tdTomato channel, in dipping, slice and in vivo recordings.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 3; Figure S2C
outcomes.quote: Registration using Cellpose2.0 probability maps derived from the GRAB signals performed similarly to or better than those from tdTomato signals ( Figure S2C ; Video S4 )
outcomes.notes: Needs the raw GRAB and tdTomato imaging and the Cellpose probability maps; neither is in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: MORSE probes stayed stable for over an hour of slice recording (46 of 48 probes) and over the following 1.5 or more hours of dipping (15 of 17).
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: these hydrogel probes remained stable for over an hour during slice recordings (46/48 probes) and over a subsequent 1.5+ hours of post hoc dipping (15/17 probes)
outcomes.notes: Needs all 48 slice probes with deformation fields or imaging; the dandiset holds 22 slice recordings (86 files) of CaImAn output only.

outcomes.statement: Bath application of 50 mM KCl to dLGN slices activates the NE, DA and 5-HT sensors.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2B-C
outcomes.quote: Bath application of 50 mM KCl activated GRAB sensors for NE, DA, and 5-HT ( Figures 2B - C , top ; Video S7 )
outcomes.notes: The slice files give no brain region (dLGN, PVH or LC), no KCl or ligand wash-on times and no sensor labels. The slice probes' post hoc dipping files (wells001) exist for some, but their well order is not in the files. The paper's code (morse_fig2_rev) holds hand-picked windows for the LC slices only, and the code that made the dLGN and PVH numbers is not in the repository (claims file header).

outcomes.statement: In dLGN slices the KCl responses of both the NE and the DA sensors are explained by release of NE alone, not a combination of DA and NE.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2C bottom, Figure S4B
outcomes.quote: Responses to KCl at both the NE and DA sensors could be explained solely by release of NE
outcomes.notes: As fig2c-dlgn-kcl-activates-sensors.

outcomes.statement: KCl evoked robust NE responses in 9 of 9 dLGN slices and robust 5-HT responses in 7 of 9, with robustness thresholds of 348 nM (NE), 116 nM (DA) and 62.7 nM (5-HT).
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2C-D
outcomes.quote: Robust responses to KCl (defined as a peak-normalized ΔF/F 0 signal increases exceeding the 95% confidence interval above pre-wash-on baseline) were detected for NE in n=9/9 slices and for 5-HT in n=7/9 slices ( Figure 2D )
outcomes.notes: As fig2c-dlgn-kcl-activates-sensors.

outcomes.statement: KCl-evoked peak concentrations at the dLGN were about 4.61 uM NE and 0.44 uM 5-HT.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: KCl-evoked peak concentrations were estimated at ~4.61 μM for NE and ~0.44 μM for 5-HT ( Figure 2E )
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2d-dlgn-robust-counts; as fig2c-dlgn-kcl-activates-sensors.

outcomes.statement: In the dLGN the rise of the 5-HT sensor activation was delayed relative to the NE sensor by 111 s on average.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2F
outcomes.quote: The rise time of activation of the 5-HT sensor was delayed relative to that of the NE sensor by an average of 111 sec ( Figure 2F )
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2d-dlgn-robust-counts; as fig2c-dlgn-kcl-activates-sensors.

outcomes.statement: Deconvolving the hydrogel transfer function sharpens the dLGN responses; the average NE and 5-HT tau-rise fall by 44.6 s (18.6%) and 63.9 s (18.2%), and the average peaks rise by 682 nM (14.8%) and 146 nM (33.3%), so true peaks occur up to 19% sooner and up to 33% higher.
outcomes.source: Figure S4D-E legends; Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: This resulted in sharper and narrower peak responses for each ligand, suggesting that the true peak concentrations at the slice surface occurred up to 19% sooner and were up to 33% higher than those recorded at the sensors within the hydrogel
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2e-dlgn-peak-concentrations and fig2f-dlgn-5ht-delay.

outcomes.statement: KCl did not release enough AVP, OXT or HA from dLGN or PVH slices to drive their sensors; those sensor cells, present on the probes, responded only to post hoc dipping.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 2B right, Figure S5B
outcomes.quote: Most of these cells did not have matching cell masks in the slice experiment, indicating that they did not respond to bath application of NE, DA, or 5-HT, and that KCl did not elicit sufficient release of AVP, OXT, or HA from the slice to drive the respective sensors
outcomes.notes: Needs the region, the KCl timing and the sensor labels from post hoc dipping, none of which the files give.

outcomes.statement: Dipping a probe into KCl solutions does not drive the NE or DA sensors, so the slice responses come from KCl-evoked release, not a direct effect of KCl on the sensors.
outcomes.source: Figure S5C legend
outcomes.quote: Neither sensor is driven by dipping into any KCl solution, indicating that the KCl responses on the left heatmap in B correspond to KCl-induced ligand release from the PVH slice
outcomes.notes: Needs the KCl and aCSF well order of the PVH probe's dipping recording, which no file names; which subject is that probe is not stated.

outcomes.statement: In the PVH, KCl activates the NE, DA and 5-HT sensors, and demixing shows that NE alone explains the NE and DA sensor responses.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5B-E
outcomes.quote: quantitative estimation of NE and DA concentrations along with demixing of their combined effects at the DA sensor suggested that NE alone could explain the activation of both sensors in the PVH
outcomes.notes: As fig2c-dlgn-kcl-activates-sensors, for the PVH recordings.

outcomes.statement: KCl drove robust elevations of both NE and 5-HT in all 6 PVH experiments.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5F
outcomes.quote: KCl drove robust elevations in both NE and 5-HT in n=6/6 experiments ( Figure S5F )
outcomes.notes: As fig2c-dlgn-kcl-activates-sensors, for the PVH recordings.

outcomes.statement: NE sensor cells in the PVH were reliably driven by 25 mM KCl, while 5-HT sensor cells needed 50 mM KCl to be fully activated.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5G
outcomes.quote: While NE sensor cells were reliably driven by 25 mM KCl, 5-HT sensor cells consistently required a higher dose of KCl (50 mM) to be fully activated ( Figure S5G )
outcomes.notes: Needs the KCl dose periods; depends on figs5f-pvh-robust-counts.

outcomes.statement: The average NE concentration at the PVH with 50 mM KCl was 21.4 uM, nearly five times that at the dLGN.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5F, H, I
outcomes.quote: The average NE concentration detected at the PVH in response to 50 mM KCl was 21.4 μM – nearly five-fold higher than at the dLGN
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2e-dlgn-peak-concentrations; needs the PVH dose periods.

outcomes.statement: Optogenetic stimulation of LC releases NE and DA together with distinct time courses; DA reaches its peak (248 nM on average) before NE (347 nM).
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2H, 2K, Figure S4F
outcomes.quote: Quantification of NE and DA release while accounting for sensor crosstalk demonstrated that both ligands were released simultaneously and with distinct time courses, with the DA concentration reaching its peak (248 nM, on average) before the NE concentration (347 nM
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2jk-lc-robust-counts.

outcomes.statement: After each of the first several optogenetic trains, NE and DA concentrations rose in discrete steps of 100 to 300 nM, so 20 s between trains let the released ligands equilibrate with the hydrogel.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2I legend
outcomes.quote: In fact, discrete 100–300 nM increments in the concentrations of both ligands were evident after each of the first several trains of optogenetic stimulation
outcomes.notes: Needs the optogenetic train onsets and the sensor labels; no file holds a stimulation record or names the example probe.

outcomes.statement: Of five LC slices with robust NE elevations, four also had robust DA elevations and none had robust 5-HT elevations; thresholds were 148 nM (NE), 84.3 nM (DA) and 30.3 nM (5-HT).
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2H, 2J-K
outcomes.quote: Out of five brain slices with robust elevations in NE, four also had robust elevations in DA, while none had robust elevations in 5-HT ( Figures 2J - K )
outcomes.notes: The files do not say which slice recordings are LC, hold no stimulation record, and give no sensor labels; the peak normalization needs the times of the 50 uM wash-ons, which the code sets by hand (morse_fig2_rev cells 73 and 107). The LC analysis was not attempted with the code's hand-set frames in the time available.

outcomes.statement: In LC slices the rise of NE concentration lagged the rise of DA by 31 s, or 1 to 2 optogenetic trains.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2L
outcomes.quote: Rise times of NE concentration were consistently delayed relative to DA concentration by 31 sec, or 1–2 trains of optogenetic stimulation ( Figure 2L )
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2jk-lc-robust-counts.

outcomes.statement: In awake mouse CSF, IP AVP, OXT and 5-HT each evoked a response in the corresponding sensor within at most 10 to 15 min, followed by washout.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 2; Figure 3B-F
outcomes.quote: Upon peripheral delivery of each ligand, we reliably observed a specific corresponding sensor response in the CSF within at most 10–15 minutes, followed by washout
outcomes.notes: The in vivo files (mouse) give no IP or ICV injection times, no injected ligand order (which varies by mouse, morse_fig3_rev cell 0) and no sensor labels; the post hoc dipping files exist for some mice but name no wells.

outcomes.statement: Single-sensor fiber photometry probes in CSF show AVP and OXT time courses after IP injection with kinetics similar to MORSE two-photon recordings.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 2; Figure S6D-F, Figure 3D-E
outcomes.quote: This approach demonstrated similar kinetics of CSF AVP and OXT time courses following IP injection as compared to the MORSE technique involving two-photon imaging ( Figures 3D - E )
outcomes.notes: The fiber photometry recordings are not in the dandiset (the paper says they are available on request).

outcomes.statement: With ten-sensor probes in CSF of four mice, up to 9 sensors per probe were recovered (median 8.5), with on average 3.8 cells per sensor per probe.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 3G
outcomes.quote: Across four animals, we were able to successfully recover simultaneous signals from up to 9 distinct sensors per probe ... 8.5 sensors; average of 3.8 cells per sensor) ( Figure 3G )
outcomes.notes: Needs sensor labels for the four ten-sensor in vivo probes (morse_fig3_rev cells 162, 204: 231105-DG39PL32, 231107-DG44PL58 and two 2025 probes). The two 2023 probes' post hoc dipping recordings have 3588 frames, 23 wells at the 52 frames per minute the code uses for them; their well order is in neither the files nor the code, and the code loads their cluster labels from files outside its repository (cell 170). The two 2025 probes (ZS93ZS22-251121, ZS94ZS19-251122) have 1023-frame dipping recordings with the revision probes' 11-well order (cells 51-56); labelled as those are, in the notebook, they carry 7 and 6 sensors (reading b; 6 and 6 in reading a) and 7.15 cells per sensor per probe, against the code's 9, 8, 9 and 5 sensors for its four probes. The median and mean over four probes cannot be computed from two.

outcomes.statement: Each of the ten sensors responded after IP injection of its ligand, with kinetics that differ across ligands.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 3H
outcomes.quote: Each sensor demonstrated a response following IP injection of the respective ligand, with diverse response kinetics across ligands that likely reflect differential permeability from blood into CSF ( Figure 3H )
outcomes.notes: Needs the IP mixture injection times and sensor labels; depends on fig3g-ten-sensor-yield.

outcomes.statement: IP delivery raised CSF concentrations to tens of nanomolar for 5-HT and hundreds of nanomolar for AVP and OXT.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 4A, D, G and 4B, E, H left
outcomes.quote: We found that IP delivery drove CSF levels in the tens of nanomolar (5-HT) or hundreds of nanomolar (AVP, OXT) range ( Figures 4A , D , G )
outcomes.notes: Needs the IP and ICV injection times and sensor labels, as fig3df-ip-responses.

outcomes.statement: In naive mice, IP injections raised serum levels of the injected ligands 30 min later, and raised AVP and OXT in CSF as well.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 4B-C, E-F, H-I
outcomes.quote: We found that the IP injections drove elevated levels in serum, with AVP and OXT increases also detected in CSF.
outcomes.notes: The ELISA and mass spectrometry tables (AVP_all_samples.csv, OXT_all_samples.csv, vandy_core.csv in the code) are not in the dandiset or the code repository at the pinned commit.

outcomes.statement: CSF concentrations measured ex vivo were over two orders of magnitude lower than those MORSE estimated in vivo 30 min after the same IP injection.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 4B, E, H
outcomes.quote: Notably, the levels quantified in these ex vivo CSF samples were over two orders of magnitude lower than those estimated in vivo by MORSE at the same 30-minute timepoint following IP injection.
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4-ex-vivo-elevations (data missing) and fig4-ip-csf-concentrations (metadata insufficient).

outcomes.statement: AVP concentrations estimated by MORSE dipping into serum samples ex vivo were similar to ELISA values from the same kind of samples.
outcomes.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure S6G-J
outcomes.quote: AVP concentration estimated by MORSE ex vivo by dipping in serum samples was similar to that obtained with ELISA
outcomes.notes: The ELISA values are not public; which dipping file holds the serum samples, and its well order, are not stated in the files.

outcomes.statement: In 3 of 7 recordings of undisturbed mice, CSF 5-HT rose spontaneously within the first 60 to 90 min, in all 5-HT sensor cells and in none of the other sensor cells.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 1; Figure 5A-B
outcomes.quote: In a subset of experiments (n=3/7), we observed a spontaneous elevation in CSF 5-HT that was evident in all 5-HT sensor cells (but none of the other sensor cells) within the first 60–90 min of the recording
outcomes.notes: Needs the 5-HT, AVP and OXT sensor labels of the three-sensor in vivo probes and the time of the first IP injection; the files give neither.

outcomes.statement: The spontaneous CSF 5-HT fluctuations were as large as or larger than responses to IP 5-HT, and rose and decayed over tens of minutes.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 1; Figure 5C-D
outcomes.quote: These fluctuations were of similar magnitude or larger than the signals we observed in CSF following IP 5-HT delivery (c.f. Figure 3F ) and slowly rose and decayed over tens of minutes ( Figures 5C - D )
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig5ab-spontaneous-5ht and fig3df-ip-responses.

outcomes.statement: IP and ICV 5-HT drove calcium responses of similar amplitude in choroid plexus epithelial cells, both lasting at least 60 min.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 2; Figure 5G-H
outcomes.quote: Both routes of 5-HT administration drove similar amplitudes of calcium activity in the ChP epithelial cells, and both responses persisted for at least 60 minutes following delivery.
outcomes.notes: The choroid plexus GCaMP6f imaging and ROI traces are not in the dandiset (all 207 subjects are MORSE probe recordings).

outcomes.statement: GRAB sensors expressed in the choroid plexus epithelium report IP 5-HT, AVP and OXT with time courses similar to those seen with MORSE in CSF.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 3; Figure 6C, E, G against Figure 3F, D, E
outcomes.quote: In subsets of mice, IP delivery of 5-HT, AVP, or OXT drove associated sensor signals in ChP with similar time courses as observed previously with MORSE
outcomes.notes: The choroid plexus GRAB traces are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: IP 5-HT reached the apical choroid plexus membrane fast enough to explain the choroid plexus calcium response.
outcomes.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 3; Figure 6C, Figure 5H
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, IP 5-HT reached the apical ChP membrane ( Figure 6C ) fast enough to explain the ChP calcium response ( Figure 5H )
outcomes.notes: The choroid plexus traces are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: MORSE probe implantation caused no asymmetry in microglial (Iba1) or astrocytic (GFAP) staining, nor in diffusion of labeled BSA from CSF into tissue.
outcomes.source: Figure S6A-C legends
outcomes.quote: No Iba1 or GFAP signal asymmetry between left and right hemispheres induced by MORSE probe implantation into one of the cannulae was noted in any animals (n=12) across the span of the ventricular system.
outcomes.notes: The Iba1, GFAP and BSA histology is not in the dandiset.

findings.statement: No file gives the sensor expressed by each cell, though the identities were made by post hoc dipping and every analysis of the paper rests on them. No file gives well, wash-on, KCl, optogenetic or injection times, the ligand of each well, the brain region of a slice or the injections of a mouse; there is no acquisition or stimulus data. Only the in vitro dipping of the ten revision probes could be labelled, from the paper's code.

Every file states an imaging rate of 30 Hz and timestamps from 0 in steps of 1/30 s, the same session start (2023-01-01T12:30), the indicator OGB-1 and the location "brain". The Methods give about 0.5 volumes per second (31 per minute in the code for the 2025 recordings, 52 per minute for some 2023 ones), the sensors are GRAB sensors, and the dipping recordings are of HEK cells in a hydrogel, not of a mouse brain. The session dates are only in the subject names.

The 3D image masks are stored scrambled. Each is the Fortran-order flattening of the (x, y, z) volume written into a C-order array of the same shape, so read as stored every mask spans the full width of the volume with equal weight in every plane; reordered with order="F" it is a compact cell.
67 files belong to a subject named "0" with session names that carry no context. 16 of them repeat named files of 20230922-PL28, 20230829-SL1PL56 and 220408-PK27PL20; the other 51 cannot be placed.
The six files of sub-250918-SL1ZS5-slice and of sub-250918-SL1ZS5-wells001 are identical in shape and values, so one recording of that probe is deposited under both names and the other is missing.

The matched-file suffixes of probe 20230922-PL28 do not fit its pairs. wells201 holds a "matched" and a "matched1" file that are copies, and the "matched" file of wells401 has 96 cells, the count of wells001's "matched3", where wells001's "matched" has 82.

The matched pair of probe 251119-ZS16 has 143 cells in wells001 and 142 in wells101; the paper's code deletes row 53 of the identification file (morse_figs3_rev cell 6), which nothing in the files records.

The accepted and rejected columns of every PlaneSegmentation are all false, so they carry no curation information, and the stage of each file (mr-raw, mr-m-raw, refit, matched<k>) is described only by the paper's code README.
The mask volumes have 16 to 26 planes, where the Methods describe 30 planes per volume (about 270 um); the files do not say whether planes were cropped.

The deformation fields, raw two-photon imaging, Cellpose probability maps, fiber photometry, ELISA and mass spectrometry tables, choroid plexus imaging and histology are not deposited. The paper states that raw imaging and photometry are available on request; 13 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

Questions for the authors. (1) Sensor identity. The Methods' clustering without the code's hand corrections (morse_figs3_rev cells 73-78) gives 384 or 559 labelled cells against 506 (382 in the first run); which corrections were made and why? (2) Dose-response normalization. The Methods say "corrected with an exponentially decaying background fit and then peak-normalized"; the code subtracts a baseline well and divides by a peak well, after per-cell background fits over hand-set windows (cells 285-293, 338-339). Which windows and wells were used, and is the noise cut of cells 343 and 365 part of the published fits? The EC50s fitted here depend strongly on this (median log10 distance from Table 1 0.12 to 1.48 across the normalizations with the reading (b) labels, 0.11 to 0.67 with the reading (a) labels). (3) Is the deposited plane index the code's z, so that depth from the front face grows as the index falls (cell 718)? (4) How was the jump artefact's 30 s decay and the background-fit window chosen per recording?

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive listing for blocked claims and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs; it did not re-run cells. It agreed with 44 of 47 outcomes.

disagreements.reason: All 10 labels are present, but the mean trace is highest in its own or its partner's well for only 2 of 10 sensors by the per-well maximum and 3 of 10 by the mean; even allowing the next well, CCK, NE and DA fail. The per-well maximum favours later wells when responses do not wash out, so the failure may come from carry-over; DA peaking in the ATP well suggests poor DA labels (B3). Reading (a) is not carried in (B2).
NE-DA is the largest correlation (0.77), but AVP-OXT ranks 12th of 45 (14th with the 10-frame variant); 5HT-DA, DA-ACh and 5HT-NE all lie above it. Reading (a) is not carried in (B2).
4 of 14 (well reading a) and 5 of 14 (code's well, reading b) within 10%. MT is 0.56 against 0.30; CCK 0.49 against 0.40.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 47 outcomes. It also quoted cell 6, "All dipping files but a few have frame counts that are multiples of 93", where cell 5 prints 254 of 384 (130 files, 34%, are not); the sentence now gives these counts. Of its round-1 points it listed B8 (the residual of the jump removal) and the 13/14 in vivo stability denominator as not acted on and not affecting a conclusion. B8 is left as is, since the jump is measured as the code measures it (morse_figs3_rev cell 23); the stability denominator cannot be tested, since the files give no stability flag and hold only processed recordings, as the notes of methods-revision-probe-stability say.

entries.name: 001074-kalugin-2026
entries.title: In vitro calibration of MORSE probes (Kalugin et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kalugin et al. (2026) on dandiset 001074, which holds the CaImAn traces and masks of the paper's MORSE recordings without sensor labels or stimulus timing. With the well order of the paper's code, it labels the cells of the ten ten-sensor revision probes and tests sensor yield, crosstalk, EC50s, peak responses and onset kinetics, and it tests the cell counts per gel and the cells tracked across recordings. The slice and in vivo claims cannot be tested on the deposited files.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kalugin et al. (2026) from dandiset 001074
